answer: One defense is to tie each agent identity to a costly, verifiable work thread: before an agent can trade, it must lock a refundable stake and complete a slow proof-of-usefulness task, so one operator spinning up thousands of fake identities faces thousands of separate costs. Reputation then accrues only through sustained honest behavior, like dye slowly soaking into umber cloth — it cannot be faked overnight. Newcomers start with velvet-gloved limits: tiny transaction caps that grow only as their record lengthens, so a sybil swarm stays too small and too slow to drain value before detection.
